title: Simplified Aircraft Motion in 1D
learningObjectives: Explain how balanced lift-weight and thrust-drag pairs maintain constant velocity in simplified 1D flight.
Determine direction of motion from the sign of thrust-minus-drag net force.
Calculate 1D acceleration as net force divided by mass for a model aircraft.

evidence.quote: By simplified motion we mean that some of the four forces acting on the aircraft are balanced by other forces

explanations.text: Simplified motion isolates one direction at a time while other opposing forces stay balanced.

evidence.quote: the weight would be balanced by the lift and the drag would be balanced by the thrust.
the aircraft will maintain at a constant cruise velocity as described by Newton’s first law of motion.

explanations.text: In balanced level flight lift balances weight and thrust balances drag, so cruise speed stays constant.

evidence.quote: If the forces become unbalanced, the aircraft will move in the direction of the greater force.
The net force is the difference between the opposing forces; lift minus weight, or thrust minus drag.

explanations.text: When opposing forces differ, the net difference drives motion in the direction of the greater force.
